name: ChEBI
rationale: Identity and structure authority, as in AntibioticMech, plus the specialized-metabolite role subtree that admits compounds no BGC covers. Release 255 holds 218,768 terms; counted directly from chebi.obo, 16,362 entities carry a role in the metabolite subtree, of which 3588 plant, 1964 bacterial, 1794 fungal and 505 marine. CC BY 4.0 quoted from the about page. No organism field and no taxid: producer information is encoded in role labels and definition prose, so ChEBI admits a record but rarely supplies a producer. The role allow-list in conf/np_roles.tsv is the scope decision and must exclude the bare metabolite roles, which would otherwise admit glucose.

name: Discovery and biosynthesis literature
rationale: No database will close the causal_graphs column. A biosynthesis or bioactivity mechanism graph is authored from primary literature with a citation per edge. Listed here so the queue does not imply that adopting sources is the whole plan.

name: LOTUS
rationale: The occurrence backbone, and the only source giving a genuine structure-organism-reference triple at scale. The 2026-04-13 frozen export was downloaded and measured: 674,454 triples, 227,319 unique InChIKeys, 37,486 organism QIDs, 91,382 reference DOIs, 175 rows with no DOI. Metadata table carries InChI, SMILES, PubChem CID, NCBI taxid, GBIF and OTT ids, and NPClassifier terms. CC0 via the Wikidata route, per Wikidata:Licensing for main-namespace structured data; the Zenodo frozen export is tagged cc-by-4.0 instead, so the route chosen decides the terms. Two cautions: manual_validation is present but empty in all 674,454 rows, so no curated subset can be selected, and the lotus.naturalproducts.net mirror is documented as unmaintained and being phased out. Occurrence only; never promote a LOTUS row to a producer claim.

name: MIBiG
rationale: The anchor source and the only one carrying an expert-curated compound-to-BGC-to-producer triple with a machine-readable experimental-evidence qualifier. Release 4.0 dump holds 3013 entries, every one with an NCBI taxid, and 5443 compound records of which 4401 have a SMILES. CC BY 4.0 stated verbatim in the paper's data-availability section and the site footer; the mibig-json GitHub repository carries no LICENSE file, so the claim rests on those two. Three traps: no InChI or InChIKey field exists anywhere, so keys are generated locally from SMILES; quality reads questionable for 2710 of 3013 and marks legacy-format entries awaiting re-curation, not doubtful science; the changelog reviewer id is the AAAA placeholder in 2988 of 3013, so a reviewer gate would admit 25 entries. Gate on active status plus loci[].evidence[].method instead. Alkaloid was removed as a biosynthetic class in 4.0 and cluster class is now PKS, NRPS, ribosomal, terpene, saccharide, other.

name: AntibioticMech
rationale: The sibling corpus, pinned at a commit and read as a committed InChIKey inventory so the join reproduces offline. Supplies related_records links and lets this corpus decline to duplicate antimicrobial mechanism, target and resistance content. Same fleet licence.

name: CyanoMetDB
rationale: Small and manually curated from primary references, which is the evidence model this corpus wants: metabolite, producer organism, primary reference, SMILES, InChIKey, sample type and whether NMR was used. Version 03 released 2024-09-28, about 3085 metabolites. The Zenodo record carries licence id cc-by-4.0. No NCBI taxids; producer attribution is often to a genus or a bloom sample rather than an axenic strain, so most rows are occurrence-grade until checked. Many congeners differ by one residue or by stereochemistry, so InChIKey deduplication against other sources will surface near-duplicates that are genuinely distinct.

name: NPClassifier
rationale: Supplies the filing decision. A biosynthesis-oriented classifier that takes a SMILES and returns pathway, superclass and class, so every record can be filed whether or not it has a gene cluster. Ontology counted from the repository: 7 pathways, 77 superclasses, 687 classes. README states verbatim that all data, models and ontology are CC0, with MIT code. Output is a prediction and must carry the model version; the API returns arrays, so a record can hold several labels per level. Run locally with a pinned model rather than depending on the API.

name: PubChem
rationale: Structures for concepts the adopted sources name without one. Public domain as a US government work, but PubChem is an aggregator and its data-source documentation states reuse conditions are set by each contributing source, so the narrow use is fetching structures for CIDs an adopted source already cross-references. Importing PubChem annotations wholesale and labelling them open is not defensible.

name: BindingDB curated records
rationale: The one cleanly licensed, structure-keyed, measured-affinity dataset in the bioactivity landscape. BindingDB's terms state verbatim that data imported from ChEMBL is CC BY-SA 3.0 while all data curated by BindingDB staff is CC BY 3.0, and the downloads are split by provenance so the two are separable. The 2026-09 articles file was downloaded and profiled: 93,712 rows over 46,304 distinct InChIKeys, with Standard InChIKey as a first-class column, UniProt per target chain, PMID, DOI, and pH and temperature per measurement, which almost nothing else carries. Two warnings from that canary. 429 rows in the articles file are labelled ChEMBL, so filter on Curation/DataSource rather than on the filename. And 93,712 is far short of the 1.6M curated points the front page advertises; the rest is patent curation whose licensing is not separately stated. Affinities embed relational operators inside the numeric cell and multi-chain targets spread UniProt ids across ~600 columns.

name: ChEMBL
rationale: The richest assay-context resource anywhere, and refused. Its FTP tree ships a LICENSE file reading Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported, so records derived from it cannot be redistributed under CC BY 4.0. Release 37 holds 24,527,044 activities over 1,970,438 assays, and already ingests CO-ADD antimicrobial screening, MMV Malaria and Pathogen Box, and DNDi. Curate-only: a lookup that guides curation from the underlying primary literature. One finding that matters beyond the licence: the natural_product flag has false positives. CHEMBL2 is prazosin, a wholly synthetic quinazoline, flagged natural_product=1 while its own np_likeness_score of -1.29 disagrees, verified by direct API call. The flag was rebuilt at release 33 from COCONUT mappings. Direct evidence that a computed or flag-based natural-product signal must never admit a record.

name: COCONUT
rationale: Blocked on aggregate relabelling, not on content. The download page states verbatim that COCONUT data is released under CC0 without any restrictions, while the project README states verbatim that every source comes with its own licence and must be reviewed. Tallying the collections column over all 738,827 rows shows the README is right: 47,475 KNApSAcK rows whose terms forbid redistribution, 81,801 NPASS rows with no stated licence, 34,748 NPAtlas rows under CC BY-NC and 30,700 CMNPD rows under CC BY-NC-SA. Adoption therefore means seeding only rows whose collections are all verified open, never the banner. Separately it cannot supply referenced occurrences at all: the organisms and dois columns are unpaired lists on the compound row. 738,827 rows over 728,421 unique InChIKeys, 37% with any organism, 33% with any DOI, about 5% revoked and needing filtering.

name: FDA GSRS / UNII
rationale: The lead that came out of the knowledge-graph cluster rather than from it. The FDA/NCATS Global Substance Registration System is US government public domain, carries structures and UNIIs, and is the resource that supplied NP-KG's constituent names in the first place. AntibioticMech already reads it, so the extractor is reusable. Useful for resolving a botanical constituent name to a substance with a structure, which is precisely the step NP-KG does not take. A UNII alone is not evidence of anything biological.

name: NPAtlas
rationale: The most painful exclusion. Best-curated microbial occurrence resource, 36,545 compounds, and a live API record carries origin_reference with both DOI and PMID plus origin_organism with an NCBI taxid and a full ancestor ladder. The terms page states verbatim that data downloaded from the Natural Products Atlas is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0, and the 3.0 paper confirms the change began at release 2024_09; releases through 2024_03 were CC BY 4.0 and would be seedable if a specific older Zenodo version's licence field is verified. No release since 2024_09. Models structure reassignments and maintains an excluded file, so a naive ingest imports superseded structures.

name: CMNPD
rationale: Marine chemistry, 31,561 compounds with sampling coordinates and 72,349 bioactivity records. Terms page states verbatim a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence, which is doubly incompatible. Frozen at v1.0 and the docs site reports it last updated six years ago. Its marine producers are frequently the collected holobiont rather than the biosynthetic organism, which is the host-symbiont trap this corpus exists to keep separate.

name: CO-ADD
rationale: The sharpest gap between branding and terms found anywhere in this landscape. The front page reads Open-access Antimicrobial Screening Database; the only terms page reserves all copyright, states that content may not be systematically downloaded, and forbids reproduction or transmission without prior written permission. No Creative Commons licence is named. Its data also reaches ChEMBL as 35 assays and 99,793 activities, where it is at least explicitly licensed, but as share-alike. The terms read like unmodified 2016 university boilerplate over a Wellcome-funded open-science project, so a CC BY request is plausible and is one of the two highest-value licence asks here. Single-concentration primary hits are inhibition percentages and must never be recorded as MICs. The operative sentence, verbatim: content "may not be systematically downloaded, retrieved or stored".

name: GNPS spectral libraries
rationale: GNPS documentation states that reference spectra contributed directly to GNPS default to CC0. But the library table types libraries as GNPS, GNPS_PROPOGATED, IMPORT and AGGREGATED and publishes no per-library licence field, so seeding needs an explicit allow-list built from the type column with the large IMPORT libraries verified individually. Spectra are detection evidence, not structures, and many library entries have no structure at all.

name: KNApSAcK
rationale: Still actively updated, 63,735 metabolites and 159,606 metabolite-species pairs as of 2026-07-03, and strong on Asian phytochemistry under-represented elsewhere. The core page states verbatim that any content cannot be re-distributed or used for commercial purposes without contacting the group. The only bulk download offered is version 1.200.03 from 2008; current data is web-only and the terms forbid scraping. A negotiated grant is conceivable because the notice invites contact, but that is a conversation, not a licence.

name: Norine
rationale: The best nonribosomal-peptide resource, with monomer-level representation. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so both NonCommercial and ShareAlike bar it; the home page's freely available to everybody continues into that licence. The compliant route is to use it as a pointer to the primary literature, which it exposes per peptide, and re-curate. Its chemistry is also where the Standard InChIKey's limits bite hardest: macrocyclic peptides, tautomers and undefined relative stereochemistry.

name: NP-KG
rationale: Assessed and refused for seeding on 2026-09-07: it carries no chemical structures at all. NP-KG v3.0.0 (June 2024, 1,089,139 nodes, 7,836,115 edges) represents natural products as a 651-class OWL extension of 613 named phytoconstituents, 460 mapped to a ChEBI class and 153 carrying only a minted napdi.org name URI whose sole superclass is CHEBI:24431, chemical entity. A grep over the extension for inchi, smiles, pubchem, unii, formula and CAS returns nothing. Every structural join would run through ChEBI, which this corpus reads directly, and the 153 name-only constituents are exactly the compounds ChEBI lacks. Licence is the second bar: the Zenodo dataset is stamped CC BY 4.0 and the code is Apache-2.0, but the graph merges PheKnowLator, whose inputs include CTD (no commercial reproduction without written permission) and DisGeNET (NC-SA), and a merge inherits its most restrictive input. The CTD terms page sits behind a human-verification gate and could not be read, so that link is medium confidence and deserves a browser check. Real value is as curator reference for plant-constituent-CYP pharmacokinetic mechanism across 31 botanicals with PubMed ids; filter by edge provenance, because its machine-read literature layer is merged into the same triple list as curated edges and scored 38.98% congruence for green tea in its own evaluation.

name: NPASS
rationale: The best structural fit for this corpus in the entire landscape, and blocked on nothing but a missing licence. Version 3.0 (2025-06-15): 204,023 natural products, 48,940 source organisms, 8,764 targets, 1,048,756 activity records including antimicrobial MICs against ESKAPE organisms, and it is natively InChIKey-keyed, which almost nothing else in the bioactivity cluster is. Homepage, about page and download page were all checked on 2026-09-07 and none carries any licence, copyright or terms statement; a third-party registry records CC-BY-NC, which is not the maintainers' word, and no statement is not permission. This is the single highest-value licence request in the landscape: one email could unblock the activity layer. Caveats if it is ever granted: it inherits from COCONUT, UNPD and TCM sources so upstream errors propagate and the same occurrence arrives by several routes, species sources are genus-level for a large fraction, and a 2023 tranche of roughly 66,600 compounds carries only estimated activity profiles that must never be read as measurements.

name: NPBS Atlas
rationale: Built for exactly this corpus's axis, compound to biological source, with 218,941 natural products split botanical, zoological, fungal, bacterial and marine. Its licence page states verbatim that access and use are freely available under CC BY-NC 4.0, while the J Cheminform article is CC BY: the article licence is not the database licence. Built largely by text mining with manual supplementation, so occurrence pairs may lack a verifiable primary reference, and TCM source annotations often name a preparation rather than a taxon.

name: PubChem BioAssay
rationale: 300,270,330 bioactivity rows over 1,980,801 assays. NCBI states that information created by or for the US government is in the public domain, but PubChem is a deposition archive and the operative licence is the depositor's, so any seeded row must record its depositor and commercial-vendor depositions should be avoided. Two traps make this curate-only for now: results are deposited on substances, some of which are mixtures, extracts or salts, and the substance-to-compound standardisation can attach an extract's activity to a single parsed constituent; and primary single-concentration screens sit beside confirmatory dose-response with no consistent flag, so an Active call is a hit, not a potency. Operational note: PubChem BioAssay carries no natural-product flag, so the natural-product slice has to be constructed rather than selected — intersect assay CIDs with the InChIKeys this corpus already holds from LOTUS, COCONUT and MIBiG, then filter by depositor. That makes it a source that thickens existing records and cannot introduce them, which suits it to M5 rather than M2.

name: StreptomeDB
rationale: Version 4.0, 8552 natural products, 3888 producer strains and 7630 curated PubMed articles, with manually curated compound-organism-reference links; the deepest Streptomyces coverage available. Neither the home page nor the download page carries a licence and the footer reads All Rights Reserved, while the NAR paper is CC BY: again the article is not the database. Worth an explicit ask, since the curated core is exactly Phase A's target. If adopted, keep the provenance flags: the same distribution mixes the curated core with 336,228 literature-mined and 398,717 pharmacophore-predicted protein relations.

name: antiSMASH database
rationale: 479,420 predicted BGC regions over 56,054 genomes, and no compound assignment anywhere, so it cannot introduce or ground a record. Its use would be indirect: expanding a known compound's producer set through KnownClusterBlast hits to MIBiG, which is a similarity claim, not identity. No data licence is published for the dumps; the code is AGPL-3.0 and the papers speak only of unrestricted access, which is about access rather than redistribution. Worth asking the maintainers, who also maintain MIBiG under CC BY.

name: BiG-FAM
rationale: CC BY 4.0 per a rel=license link on the site. Gene cluster families would let a producer claim generalize across strains, but it is frozen on 2020 data and MIBiG 2.0, and its documented bulk-download URL returned nothing. Reference only until it is refreshed.

name: ClassyFire and ChemOnt
rationale: Bespoke terms requiring permission for commercial redistribution. NPClassifier is CC0 and biosynthesis-oriented, which suits this corpus better anyway, so ChemOnt is refused rather than queued. This also means dropping ChemOnt strings that arrive inside otherwise-CC BY records from MassBank.

name: DrugCentral
rationale: CC BY-SA 4.0, so share-alike bars it, and its public dump is still the 2023 release. Drugs@FDA plus GSRS covers the same regulatory ground under public-domain terms, which is the route AntibioticMech already took.

name: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
rationale: The cleanest licence in the whole landscape and among the dirtiest data. Its about page states verbatim that contents are made available under a Creative Commons CC0 public domain dedication, deposited with a DOI through USDA Ag Data Commons. But activity labels are frequently attributed to a plant and then associated with its constituent chemicals, which is the herb-level-indication trap by construction, and many entries carry no units, no assay and no dose. CC0 makes it seedable and the evidence rules make most of it unusable as a BioactivityObservation. Frozen; developed 1992-2016.

name: ENPKG
rationale: The only genuinely natural-product-specific knowledge graph found. Sample-centric LC-MS/MS from plant extract collections, with molecular networking, in-silico annotation and links to Wikidata and LOTUS. Its compound nodes are putative structural annotations of mass features, ranked by score, so it says what was probably in one extract rather than what an organism is known to produce. Hypothesis-grade, therefore a curation lead and never a seed. Deposits are licensed individually, CC BY on some and CC0 on others, so even reference use needs a per-deposit check; the code is GPL/AGPL, which matters only if the pipeline were vendored.

name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to PHARMACOLOGY
rationale: Expert-curated ligand-target pharmacology with a natural-product slice. Refused twice over: the database is ODbL and its content CC BY-SA 4.0, both share-alike, and bulk downloads have moved behind a login. Curator reference at best, and awkward even for that.

name: KEGG
rationale: Secondary-metabolite biosynthesis maps. KEGG states it is not a public database and requires a commercial licence. Refused.

name: MassBank and MoNA
rationale: MoNA is CC BY 4.0 by default per its own application; MassBank EU carries a mandatory per-record LICENSE tag that defaults to CC BY. Per-record means the distribution of values across the roughly 139,000 records must be computed before ingest and any non-CC BY or non-CC0 value quarantined. Record counts differ by release train (119,845 in the 2026 paper, 134,756 in the deployed instance, 139,006 from the count endpoint), so never quote one without naming its source. Note MassBank records carry ChemOnt strings, which ClassyFire's terms restrict; drop those and keep NPClassifier.

name: MetaCyc and BioCyc
rationale: Secondary-metabolite pathways with enzyme steps, which is what biosynthetic_pathway wants. Requires a subscription the site describes as costing at least 5000 dollars. Not seedable and not usable as a curation crib without a data licence.

name: NP-MRD
rationale: Natural-product NMR reference data, which would be strong structural evidence. CC BY-NC 4.0, so not seedable. Same treatment as Norine: a pointer to the primary report.

name: Open Targets Platform
rationale: Licence page states verbatim that the Platform is marked with CC0 1.0. The same page then enumerates 50+ integrated sources, several of them CC BY-SA, ChEMBL and Human Protein Atlas among them. So Open Targets is usable for its own aggregation and must never be a laundering route for ChEMBL bioactivity, which its drug and mechanism-of-action datasets are substantially derived from. Association scores are computed and are not bioactivity, and its associations are gene-level rather than compound-level, so it closes little here.

name: Paired Omics Data Platform
rationale: CC BY 4.0, verified from the app bundle and submission terms, and conceptually ideal: it links BGCs to mass spectra. But it holds only 117 BGC-to-MS2 links in total, so it closes almost nothing at present. Revisit if it grows.

name: Rhea
rationale: CC BY 4.0, quoted from the FTP LICENSE.txt after the help page returned 403. The open route to representing a pathway step as a reaction with ChEBI participants, joinable to UniProt through the enzyme. Only useful once curated pathways exist, so it sits behind M6.
